detail.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)). I cannot set labels from a fork; suggested: `cat-bugfix`, `area:sparse_attention`, `mod-cutedsl`, `orig-nv-eng`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

Fix two non-finite cases in the CSA compressor's ratio=128 forward (`csa/compressor/compressor_sm100_r128.py`), whose
window softmax is computed in chunks and merged:

- A chunk with a NaN or +inf score was dropped by the merge, so the output was finite where the eager softmax gives NaN.
  The merge now skips only empty chunks (`den == 0`).
- A -inf position (for example a masked APE row) seen before any finite position computed `exp(-inf - -inf)` = NaN, so
  the output was NaN or wrong where the eager softmax gives that position weight 0. The running max now starts at the
  lowest finite fp32 instead of -inf.

On finite inputs the output is bitwise unchanged and the kernel time is unchanged. Adds a test over every forward
schedule bucket.

## Why

Each CTA splits a row's window into `tchunks` chunks; a chunk keeps a running `(m, den, acc)` and the CTA merges the
chunk partials in a fixed order. `docs/fe-oss-apis/csa.md` (Numerics, ratio=128, item 3) states that the kernels
reproduce the fp32 eager reference's non-finite propagation.

**NaN chunk dropped.** The merge skipped a partial with `if d2 > 0`, to ignore the empty previous-block half of a
segment's first block. A chunk that saw a NaN score, or a +inf score (`exp(inf - inf)`), has `den = NaN`, which also fails
`> 0`. The NaN was lost unless it was in the first chunk. Repro: one NaN or +inf score at block 1, own-half position 100,
column 0; compare `out[1, 0]` with the fp32 eager softmax:

| coff, d, blocks | develop, NaN score | develop, +inf score | this PR | eager |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 128, 64 | 0.4688 | 0.4688 | NaN | NaN |
| 2, 128, 64 | -0.3105 | -0.3105 | NaN | NaN |
| 1, 512, 64 | 0.0618 | 0.0618 | NaN | NaN |
| 1, 128, 300 | 0.1318 | 0.1318 | NaN | NaN |
| 2, 512, 2000 | 0.0425 | 0.0425 | NaN | NaN |

The merge now tests `d2 != 0`: an empty chunk has `den == 0` exactly and is still skipped, and a NaN partial is merged.

**-inf before the first finite position.** The running max started at -inf. In the online loop a -inf position does not
update the max (`s > m` is false), so it computes `exp(s - m) = exp(-inf - -inf) = NaN`; in the two-phase loop a chunk
whose positions are all -inf has max -inf and the same NaN. With APE row 0 set to -inf (the first position of every
window masked), against the fp32 eager reference, which is finite everywhere:

| coff, d, blocks | develop: NaN outputs | develop: max abs error on the finite ones | this PR: NaN outputs / max abs error |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 128, 64 | 8192 / 8192 | - | 0 / 0.0039 |
| 2, 128, 64 | 8064 / 8192 | 0.776 | 0 / 0.0032 |
| 1, 512, 300 | 153600 / 153600 | - | 0 / 0.0077 |
| 1, 128, 2000 (two-phase) | 0 | 0.0053 | 0 / 0.0053 |

The two-phase bucket is not affected here because its first chunk's max is finite. A chunk after the first whose
positions are all -inf had `den = NaN` and was dropped by `d2 > 0`, which happened to give the eager result; with the
merge fix alone it would make the output NaN, so both changes are needed (see Testing). The running max now starts at the lowest finite fp32: a -inf
position seen before any finite one contributes `exp(-inf) = 0`, a chunk of only -inf positions ends with `den == 0` and
is skipped by the merge, and an all -inf window gives `0 / 0` = NaN, as the eager softmax does. On finite inputs the
first finite position rescales the empty `(0, 0)` partial by `exp(lowest - s) = 0`, exactly as `exp(-inf - s)` did, so
the outputs are bitwise the same. A per-element `m == -inf ? 0 : m` guard in the exp argument fixes the same cases, but it
measured up to 12% slower in the online-loop buckets (c2 d128 1024 blocks: 41.9 -> 47.0 us), so this PR uses the initial
value instead.

The other CSA kernels apply the same rule correctly already: the ratio=128 backward and the ratio 2 / 4 kernels take the
max over the whole window before the exp and sum every partial without a skip, which matches the eager softmax for a
NaN, a +inf, a -inf at any position and an all -inf window.

## Related issues

None filed. #1605 (merged) added the deterministic dAPE path to the ratio=128 backward in the same file; this PR is based
on develop after it and touches only the forward kernel.

## API and compatibility impact

No API change.

- Finite inputs: the forward output is bitwise identical to develop on 40 configurations (coff 1 / 2 x d 128 / 512 x
  64, 300 and 1024 blocks, a ragged `[1023, 2048, 509]` pack and an edge pack `[127, 8192, 0, 129, 128, 3, 515, 1024]`,
  5 static padding rows, two seeds, one of them with 4x score scale).
- Kernel time on B200 (torch.profiler device time, median of 7 x 50 launches, develop and this PR alternated A/B/A/B in
  separate processes on the same GPU) is unchanged within 0.1 us in every bucket:

  | coff, d | 64 blocks | 300 blocks | 1024 blocks |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1, 128 | 6.24 / 6.24 us | 10.21 / 10.21 | 15.30 / 15.28 |
  | 2, 128 | 7.98 / 7.98 | 13.21 / 13.22 | 41.95 / 41.97 |
  | 1, 512 | 9.52 / 9.51 | 28.40 / 28.36 | 74.68 / 74.69 |
  | 2, 512 | 12.02 / 12.03 | 52.93 / 52.95 | 123.57 / 123.49 |

  (develop / this PR, first round; the second round matches.)

## Testing

B200 (sm_100), driver 615.71, CUDA 13.4, torch 2.14, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0.dev0. The tree under test is this branch's
`python/cudnn` (develop 70a1791c plus this commit) over the nvidia-cudnn-frontend 1.31.0 wheel's compiled module; the
change is Python-only.

`test_r128_forward_special_values_match_eager` runs 5 cases in every forward schedule bucket (c1d512-small and
c2d128-large run their default bucket's schedule and are left out; the two d=512 large packs are L1): one NaN score, one
+inf score, a -inf APE row at a chunk start (row 64), -inf APE rows 64-127 (whole chunks without a finite position), and
-inf in every APE row. The output's NaN mask must equal the fp32 eager reference's, and the finite elements must stay
within the suite's r128 tolerance (max abs <= 1.6e-2, differing elements <= max(1, 0.1%)).

- RED, develop's `python/cudnn` with this branch's tests: `pytest compressed_sparse_attention` -> 23 failed, 170 passed,
  1 skipped (the NaN, +inf and chunk-start cells; the two-phase bucket's chunk-start cell passes on develop);
  with `-m "L0 or L1"` and `-k special_values` -> 29 failed, 21 passed.
- The merge change alone (develop plus `d2 != 0` only): 19 failed, all of them -inf cells, including the two-phase
  bucket's whole-chunk cell, so the test needs both changes.
- GREEN: `pytest compressed_sparse_attention` -> 193 passed, 1 skipped; `-m "L0 or L1 or L2 or L3 or L4"` -> 213 passed,
  1 skipped (develop: 163 passed, 1 skipped).
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: black, black-jupyter and SPDX passed with no changes.

`docs/fe-oss-apis/csa.md` (Numerics, item 3) now states the rule for non-finite inputs and names the test.

cc @Anerudhan @icavan

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

detail.title: CSA ratio=128 forward: propagate NaN / +inf scores and give -inf positions weight 0 in the chunk merge

files.patch:
@@ -91,7 +91,10 @@ assume the ratio \{2, 4\} guarantees at ratio=128):
      fp32 max — its forward chunk partials are un-normalized (up to `2 · ratio ×`
      the reference's normalized weighted sums), so e.g. uniform-score inputs with
      `|kv|` within a factor `~2 · ratio` of fp32 max return ±Inf where the eager
-     reference is still finite.
+     reference is still finite. Non-finite inputs follow the same rule wherever
+     they fall in the forward's window chunks: a NaN or +Inf `score + ape` at one
+     window position makes that output NaN, and a -Inf position (a masked one)
+     gets weight 0 (`test_r128_forward_special_values_match_eager`).
 
   On inputs whose fp32 intermediates stay finite in BOTH evaluation orders — the
   eager reference's and the fused kernels' (which saturate earlier, see 3.) —

@@ -127,9 +127,10 @@
 # issued instructions at the instruction-bound buckets (B200 SASS audit).
 # exp(-inf) == +0 and NaN -> NaN are preserved by ex2.approx; ftz flushes only
 # sub-2^-126 results, which softmax consumes as exact zeros (den >= exp(0) = 1 always
-# survives).
+# survives in a window with a finite position).
 _L2E_HI = 1.4426950216293335  # fp32(log2(e))
 _L2E_LO = 1.925963033500011e-08  # fp32(log2(e) - _L2E_HI); residual ~4e-16
+_LOWEST_F32 = -3.4028234663852886e38  # lowest finite fp32: the forward's initial running max
 
 
 # ``cute.math.exp2``'s ``approx``/``ftz`` keywords are newer than the
@@ -252,11 +253,16 @@ def _compressor_fwd_r128_kernel(
         #
         # Both forms produce a (m, den, acc) partial with identical merge semantics;
         # both are run-to-run bitwise deterministic.
+        #
+        # The running max starts at the lowest finite fp32, not -inf: a -inf position
+        # seen before any finite one (a masked position, or a chunk with no finite
+        # position) then contributes exp(-inf) == 0, as in the eager softmax, instead of
+        # exp(-inf - -inf) == NaN. On finite inputs the output is bitwise unchanged.
         fr_m = cute.make_rmem_tensor((vec,), cutlass.Float32)
         fr_d = cute.make_rmem_tensor((vec,), cutlass.Float32)
         fr_a = cute.make_rmem_tensor((vec,), cutlass.Float32)
         for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(vec):
-            fr_m[j] = cutlass.Float32(_NEG_INF)
+            fr_m[j] = cutlass.Float32(_LOWEST_F32)
             fr_d[j] = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
             fr_a[j] = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
 
@@ -315,7 +321,8 @@ def _compressor_fwd_r128_kernel(
                         m_old = cutlass.Float32(fr_m[j])
                         if s > m_old:
                             # New running max: rescale den/acc by exp(m_old - s); the
-                            # first valid position rescales by exp(-inf) == 0 exactly.
+                            # first finite position rescales the empty (0, 0) partial by
+                            # exp(lowest - s) == 0 exactly.
                             if cutlass.const_expr(fastexp):
                                 scale = _exp_fast(m_old - s)
                             else:
@@ -349,9 +356,10 @@ def _compressor_fwd_r128_kernel(
         if col < ncol:
             if tidy == 0:
                 # Fixed-order serial merge of the tchunks partials per dim. Empty
-                # partials (den == 0: the skipped previous-block half) are ignored;
-                # every row has at least one valid position (the own half), so the
-                # merged den is >= 1 and the final division is safe.
+                # partials (den == 0: the skipped previous-block half, or a chunk
+                # whose positions are all -inf) are ignored; a NaN partial is merged.
+                # A window with a finite position has a merged den >= 1; an all -inf
+                # window gives 0 / 0 = NaN, as the eager softmax does.
                 cvec = col * vec
                 fr_o = cute.make_rmem_tensor((vec,), cutlass.BFloat16)
                 for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(vec):
@@ -361,14 +369,16 @@ def _compressor_fwd_r128_kernel(
                     for t in cutlass.range_constexpr(1, tchunks):
                         slot = (t * threads_x + tidx) * vec + j
                         d2 = cutlass.Float32(sD[slot])
-                        if d2 > 0:
+                        # A NaN partial (a NaN or +inf score in that chunk) is merged, so the output is NaN.
+                        if d2 != cutlass.Float32(0.0):
                             m2 = cutlass.Float32(sM[slot])
                             a2 = cutlass.Float32(sA[slot])
                             mn = m
                             if m2 > mn:
                                 mn = m2
-                            # exp(-inf - mn) == 0 handles a still-empty running
-                            # partial; both-empty never reaches here (d2 > 0).
+                            # The running partial may still be empty (den == acc == 0,
+                            # m the initial lowest finite value); den and acc stay 0
+                            # whatever exp(m - mn) is.
                             s1 = cute_math.exp(m - mn)
                             s2 = cute_math.exp(m2 - mn)
                             den = _ffma_rn(den, s1, _fmul_rn(d2, s2))

@@ -364,6 +364,73 @@ def test_replay_determinism_r128():
         assert torch.allclose(runs[0][3], other[3], rtol=0, atol=1e-3)
 
 
+def _fused_forward(kv, score, ape, cu, cuc, total_comp, ratio, d, coff):
+    """Forward only through the fused wrapper; returns out as (total_comp, 1, d)."""
+    compressor = _import_compressor()
+    total = kv.shape[0]
+    out = compressor.csa_compressor_forward_wrapper(
+        kv.view(total, -1), score.view(total, -1), ape, cu, cuc, ratio=ratio, head_dim=d, coff=coff, total_comp=total_comp
+    )["out"]
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return out.view(total_comp, 1, d)
+
+
+# Every ratio=128 forward schedule: (coff, d, nb) per bucket (small <= 128 rows, default, large >= 1024 rows).
+# c1d512-small and c2d128-large run their default bucket's schedule; the d=512 large packs are L1.
+_R128_FWD_BUCKETS = [
+    pytest.param(1, 128, 64, id="c1d128-small", marks=pytest.mark.L0),
+    pytest.param(1, 128, 300, id="c1d128-default", marks=pytest.mark.L0),
+    pytest.param(1, 128, 1024, id="c1d128-large-twophase", marks=pytest.mark.L0),
+    pytest.param(2, 128, 64, id="c2d128-small", marks=pytest.mark.L0),
+    pytest.param(2, 128, 300, id="c2d128-default", marks=pytest.mark.L0),
+    pytest.param(1, 512, 300, id="c1d512-default", marks=pytest.mark.L0),
+    pytest.param(1, 512, 1024, id="c1d512-large", marks=pytest.mark.L1),
+    pytest.param(2, 512, 64, id="c2d512-small", marks=pytest.mark.L0),
+    pytest.param(2, 512, 300, id="c2d512-default", marks=pytest.mark.L0),
+    pytest.param(2, 512, 1024, id="c2d512-large", marks=pytest.mark.L1),
+]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "case",
+    [
+        "nan_score",  # one NaN score, not in its window's first chunk
+        "posinf_score",  # one +inf score, not in its window's first chunk
+        "neginf_ape_chunk_start",  # -inf APE row 64: a masked position that starts a chunk
+        "neginf_ape_whole_chunk",  # -inf APE rows 64..127: chunks with no finite position
+        "neginf_ape_all",  # every position masked: the eager softmax is NaN everywhere
+    ],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("coff,d,nb", _R128_FWD_BUCKETS)
+def test_r128_forward_special_values_match_eager(coff, d, nb, case):
+    """ratio=128 forward with special values at single window positions, in every schedule bucket.
+
+    The forward merges per-chunk softmax partials. The output's NaN pattern must equal the fp32 eager
+    reference's, and the finite elements must stay within the r128 tolerance contract: a NaN or +inf
+    position makes its output NaN, and a -inf position gets weight 0 wherever it falls in a chunk.
+    """
+    _require_sm100()
+    ratio = 128
+    kv, score, ape, cu, cuc, total_comp, _ = _make_inputs([nb * ratio], d, ratio, coff)
+    if case.endswith("_score"):
+        # Block 1, own-half position 100, column 0 of the own-half projection.
+        score[ratio + 100, 0, d if coff == 2 else 0] = float("nan") if case == "nan_score" else float("inf")
+    else:
+        rows = {"neginf_ape_chunk_start": slice(64, 65), "neginf_ape_whole_chunk": slice(64, 128), "neginf_ape_all": slice(0, ratio)}[case]
+        ape[rows] = float("-inf")
+
+    out = _fused_forward(kv, score, ape, cu, cuc, total_comp, ratio, d, coff).float()
+    ref = _eager_pool(kv, score, ape, cu, cuc, total_comp, ratio, d, coff, mode="fp32").float()
+    assert torch.equal(out.isnan(), ref.isnan()), (int(out.isnan().sum()), int(ref.isnan().sum()))
+    if case.endswith("_score"):
+        assert ref[1, 0, 0].isnan()
+    finite = ~ref.isnan()
+    if finite.any():
+        diff = (out[finite] - ref[finite]).abs()
+        assert diff.max().item() <= 1.6e-2, diff.max().item()
+        assert (diff > 0).sum().item() <= max(1, int(0.001 * diff.numel()))
+
+
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # ratio=128 dispatch envelope: every shipped schedule bucket
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `9b500110b040` against base `70a1791c8653`.

Thank you for your contribution! Both changes are needed and work together: the finite initial maximum keeps masked -Inf positions from poisoning an otherwise valid partial, while den != 0 preserves NaN partials during merging. I found no remaining approval-blocking issue in this diff and independently reproduced the old dropped-NaN behavior.

Validation: Reviewed all three changed files against base 70a1791c8653, including both online/two-phase accumulation, empty previous-block chunks, merge ordering, all-masked windows, and the documented numerical contract. Precheck produced no candidates; this scalar change adds no synchronization or storage ownership changes. Exact-head Python sources on native SM100 (148 SMs), CuTeDSL 4.8.0: 213 passed, 1 skipped in the complete CSA compressor suite with L0-L4 enabled. The skip requires two visible supported GPUs. This includes all 50 new non-finite cases, existing finite-input and deterministic-backward checks, and CUDA-graph tests. The supported CuTeDSL 4.6.2 floor also passed all 50 new non-finite schedule cases (164 unrelated cases deselected, no skips), confirming the NaN comparison semantics on that version. Independent base/head probes across four configurations reproduced the old finite output for a NaN score in a later chunk; every head result matched the eager reference's NaN pattern. Finite inputs were bitwise identical between base and head in all four configurations. 24 additional changed-input graph replays passed: NaN/+Inf at the first and last own-window positions, one remaining finite APE position, and lowest-finite FP32 scores, across online and two-phase schedules and coff=1/2 with D128/D512 coverage. Four finite-input ABBA spot checks showed no material regression: GPU replay remained approximately 9.3, 12.2, 24.2, and 18.6 us for (coff,D,blocks)=(1,128,64), (2,128,64), (1,128,1024), and (2,512,64). Cached internal-launcher CPU submission remained 4.78-4.86 us. These CPU measurements cover run_fwd_r128, not the full wrapper or an application. Outputs were checked after timings.

Limitations: Native validation covers SM100 only. CI and other platforms remain separate evidence; the spot checks are not serving-level benchmarks. A compatible existing native FE extension was reused for this Python-only change; no changed binding is involved.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
